title: The Dragon Hatchling: The Missing Link between the Transformer and Models of the Brain
relevance: Primary source for this project's core concept. Defines σ(i,j), the Hebbian synaptic-strength update this project's toy simulation directly implements, and reports the 'tension relaxes over time unless reinforced' decay behavior.

title: A Modern Self-Referential Weight Matrix That Learns to Modify Itself
authors: Kazuki Irie, Imanol Schlag, Róbert Csordás, Jürgen Schmidhuber
relevance: Extends the fast-weight / Hebbian-style associative memory line of work that BDH's synaptic memory formalism builds on: weights that are written and read dynamically at inference time rather than fixed after training.

title: Gated Linear Attention Transformers with Hardware-Efficient Training
authors: Songlin Yang, Bailin Wang, Yikang Shen, Rameswar Panda, Yoon Kim
relevance: A recent linear-attention variant that, like BDH-GPU, reframes attention as an incrementally updated fast-weight state rather than a full pairwise comparison — relevant context for why sparsity and gating (used by BDH) matter for controlling what gets 'remembered' vs forgotten.

title: Learning to (Learn at Test Time): RNNs with Expressive Hidden States
authors: Yu Sun, Xinhao Li, Karan Dalal, Jiarui Xu, et al.
relevance: Tests a related idea — a fixed-size recurrent state updated by a local learning rule at inference/test time — directly relevant to the claim that fixed-shape recurrent state can substitute for a growing memory, and to what such state can and cannot retain (interference / capacity).
